profiles.name: Chantilly Geigle
profiles.description:
Chantilly Geigle crossed the line at Fort Benning, Georgia during the September 2002 SOA Watch vigil to close the U.S. Army School of the Americas / WHINSEC. Sentenced to 6 months in federal custody.

Each year on the November anniversary of the assassination of six Jesuits, their housekeeper, and her daughter at the University of Central America in San Salvador in 1989, peace activists gather at the gates of Fort Benning, Georgia, site of the U.S. Army School of the Americas / Western Hemisphere Institute for Security Cooperation (WHINSEC), to commemorate the dead and to call for the school's closure. Hundreds have crossed the line onto the base over four decades of vigils; many have served federal sentences ranging from 30 days to a year for trespass.
profiles.finding: Prison newsletter corroboration; Portland healthcare-provider namesake unlinked; no verified image.

profiles.name: Mike Pasquale
profiles.description: Mike Pasquale was a Syracuse peace activist and program director at the Family Center who crossed onto Fort Benning on November 18, 2001 during a School of the Americas Watch protest. Federal prisoner records listed him as Michaele Pasquale, number 91102-020. He was convicted of federal trespass on July 12, 2002 and sentenced to six months in prison and a $1,000 fine. Pasquale served the sentence at Federal Prison Camp Allenwood from September 10, 2002 to March 7, 2003.
profiles.finding: Syracuse Peace Council archive corroboration; racing official and obituary namesakes unlinked.

profiles.name: Mohammed Rafiq Butt
profiles.description:
Mohammed Rafiq Butt was a 55-year-old Pakistani national held on immigration charges during the detentions following September 11, 2001. He died at Hudson County Correctional Center in New Jersey on October 23, 2001. Human Rights Watch reported that the preliminary autopsy attributed his death to unspecified heart problems and that he had no attorney when he died.

His cellmate told Human Rights Watch that detainees helped Butt submit repeated requests for medical attention during the approximately ten days before his death, without a doctor seeing him in response. The report also noted that he had received antibiotics for a gum infection earlier that month. Human Rights Watch sought an investigation into his death and questioned the adequacy of his care. His case concerns immigration detention and treatment during the national-security dragnet; the sources cited here do not establish that he was prosecuted for personal political activism.
profiles.finding: Government hearing and WSWS corroborate death in detention; no verified portrait.
